JUDGMENT

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 22 of the Employees Compensation Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest @ 12% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

The substance of Petition averments as stated in the petition is as under:
The deceased namely Nadim Pasha was working under the Respondent No.1 as a driver and was earning Rs.25,000/-per month.

That on 10.06.2020 as per the instruction of Respondent No.1, the deceased Nadim Pasha was driving the Tempo/Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-0657, on Mumbai express highway road and at 3.30 a.m., when he reached near Uras Toll gate, at that time, one Trailer bearing No.RJ- 14-GG-0642 was proceeding in front of his vehicle and the driver of the trailer has suddenly slow down his vehicle without giving any signal or proper indicator and deceased Nadim Pasha tried to avoid hit against the trailer, but, he could not control and dashed against the trailer from the backside.

As a result, the deceased Nadim Pasha had sustained severe head injury and other injuries to all over the body and he was immediately taken to the Sapna hospital, wherein doctor has examined the Nadim Pasha and declared SCCH - 15 4 ECA.No.57/2020 as dead.
Thereafter, the Postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to his family members.
The Petitioners had spent Rs.80,000/- towards funeral and last rites and Rs.50,000/- for transportation of dead body and other expenses.
Prior to the date of incident, the deceased Nadim Pasha was hale and healthy.
The Petitioners were solely depending on the income of the deceased and he was the only earning member of their family.

Due to this incident, the whole family of the Ayesha Banu vs Waseem Khan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185218097/
2
Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Tempo/Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG- 0657.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, this Petition.

3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection Statements to the main Petition.

SCCH - 15 5 ECA.No.57/2020 The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement has admitted that the deceased Nadim Pasha was working under him as a driver in Tempo/Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG- 0657 and he was paying a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month to the deceased Nadim Pasha.
Further he admitted that deceased Nadim Pasha was died during the course of employment under him.
Further he admitted that he is the RC owner of the Tempo/Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG- 0657 and said vehicle was insured with the Respondent No.2.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement has denied the employer and employee relationship between the deceased Nadim Pasha and the Respondent No.1 and also denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and death of the deceased in the said accident.

Further it contended that deceased / driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence and willfully entrusted the vehicle to SCCH - 15 6 ECA.No.57/2020 the said driver and thereby he committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it contended that the Tempo/Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-0657 was not having valid permit to ply in Maharashtra as on the date of accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, it has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are Legal heir of deceased Nadim Pasha?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove the employee and employer relation between Nadim Pasha and Respondent No.1?
3. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the accident occurred during the course of employment under the Respondent No.1 and as a result Nadim Pasha succumbed to injuries?

It is the contentions of the Petitioners that they are the Legal heirs of the deceased Nadim Pasha.
PW.1 in her chief-examination stated that she is the wife and the Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and the Petitioner No.4 is the mother of deceased Nadim Pasha.

In order to prove the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased, they have relied on Ex.P.1 to 5 i.e.,
Aadhaar cards of Petitioner No.1, 4 and deceased and Birth certificates of Petitioner No.2 and 3.
Ex.P1 is the Aadhaar card of the Petitioner No.1.
Ex.P4 is the Aadhaar card of the Petitioner No.4 which shows that she is the wife of the Akmal Pasha.
Ex.P5 is the Aadhaar card of the deceased Nadim Pasha which also shows the name of his father as Akmal Pasha.
It is to be noted here that Police documents does not show father name of the deceased Nadim Pasha.

But, Ex.P15 i.e., Death Certificate of the deceased Nadim Pasha shows his father as Akmal Pasha and date of death was 10.06.2020 and place of death is Express Highway Road, Khandala, SCCH - 15 9 ECA.No.57/2020 Pune, Maharashtra.
So, it is clear that the name of the husband of PW.1 is Nadim Pasha and said deceased Nadim Pasha is the son of Akmal Pasha and his death occurred at Khandala.

Therefore,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners are the wife, children and mother of the deceased Nadim Pasha.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative".
8. ISSUE No.2 and 3:
Both Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.

The Petitioners claims that the deceased Nadim Pasha was the driver under the Respondent No.1 and they invoked Sec.22 of Workmen Compensation Act and they have to prove the relationship of the deceased Nadim Pasha with the Respondent No.1 that as on the date of the incident, there Ayesha Banu vs Waseem Khan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185218097/
4 existed employer and employee relationship between the Respondent No.1 and deceased Nadim Pasha.

It is the condition precedent that the LRs of deceased employee can SCCH - 15 10 ECA.No.57/2020 claim compensation from his employer subject to proving the relationship between the deceased and his employer.
9. Second most important aspect of the matter is that, incident should have occurred during the course of employment with his employer.

The PW.1 has re-iterated the fact in her chief examination that her husband met with an accident on 10.06.2020 while he was working under Respondent No.1.

Ex.P12 is the Certificate issued by the Sapna Hospital which shows that Mr. Nadim Pasha taken to his clinic by the Police for the alleged history of Road Traffic Accident around 3.30 a.m. and he was brought dead and declared death at 8.10 a.m.
Ex .P-13 and Ex.P14 are the IMV reports which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P15 is the Death Certificate which shows that the Nadim Pasha was died at Express Highway Road, Khandala, Lonavala, Maharashtra.

He admitted that in the Charge-sheet it was mentioned as Nadim Pasha was driving the vehicle.

In the cross- examination he also admitted that, at the time of accident, the Insurance policy in respect of Tempo bearing Reg.
KA-01- AG-0657 was in force.

It is pertinent note here that the Respondent No.1 in his Written Statement admitted the employer and employee relationship between himself and SCCH - 15 14 ECA.No.57/2020 deceased Nadim Pasha and also admitted that while said Nadim Pasha was under his employement, he met with an accident and he died.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the employer and employee relationship between the Respondent No.1 and deceased Nadim Pasha and during the course of his employment under Respondent No.1,
he was died.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 in the "Affirmative".
16. ISSUE No.4: PW.1 has deposed the age of the deceased Nadim Pasha was 41 years at the time of accident.
PW.1 has produced Aadhaar card of the deceased Nadim Pasha at Ex.P5 which shows his birth year was 1979.
The alleged incident has taken place on 10.06.2020.
Therefore, at the time of the accident, the deceased Nadim Pasha was aged 42 years.

17. Though the Respondent No.1 stated in his Written Statement that he was paying Rs.20,000/- as a monthly salary to the deceased Nadim Pasha, he has not produced SCCH - 15 15 ECA.No.57/2020 any documents in this regard and he has not stepped into the witness box to lead evidence.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.14,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

18. The Factor applicable to the deceased as per the Schedule IV of the Employees Compensation Act 1923 is 181.37.
19.
In the instant case this tribunal has held that the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.14,500/-.
In order to calculate loss of dependency, 50% of the monthly income of the deceased shall have to be taken into consideration.

If 50% of the monthly income of the deceased is deducted,
the remaining amount would be Rs.7,250/- (50% of Rs.14,500/-).
If Rs.7,250/- is multiplied by the Factor 181.37, the amount would be Rs.13,14,932.50/-.

20 . Further, as per the detailed discussion made in the above Issues, this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the deceased Nadim Pasha was worked under the Respondent SCCH - 15 16 ECA.No.57/2020 No.1 and during the course of employment, he died.
Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The policy of the offending vehicle is valid at the time of incident.
Hence, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
